value.body: Transportation engineers plan and design roads, junctions, highways and transit systems so traffic moves safely and efficiently. They work in infrastructure consultancies, government departments and metro and highway projects, and the day involves traffic studies, design on software, reports and coordinating with project teams.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech in Civil Engineering; often M.Tech in Transportation Engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: AutoCAD, Civil 3D or MX Road, traffic simulation software, IRC codes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many design roles prefer an M.Tech in transportation engineering, often reached through GATE. B.Tech graduates also start as trainee highway or traffic engineers in infrastructure consultancies.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Highway geometric design to IRC codes

value.title: At a glance
items: Much work is tied to government highway and metro projects.
Common next steps: senior highway engineer, traffic planner, or project manager.
Field surveys alternate with office-based design.
